issues.description: The programs require hand-collected CSV/Excel inputs, supplementary prepared tables and an earlier Dealscan–Compustat link. These files are absent from the assigned archive, so author delivery/specification is needed before data construction.

Entry programs invoke %WRDS/remote blocks, but support macro loading is not shown in the entries; remote librefs/home paths, SAS Connect, WT remote include path and blank DVW/SLACK paths need confirmation.

The SAS programs prepare data and say subsequent analysis is separate. The appendix describes Stata MI/other analyses, but no executable analysis program or complete per-table procedure is supplied. No compatible prepared-analysis bypass supports analysis_only.

All frozen edges are reviewed, but full history/field compatibility, macro-expanded IBES IDSUM/actual routes, legacy aliases and remote configuration remain unresolved. One-row probes establish columns/readability only, not history. Known stage order is Compile DealData before DVW.

evidence.description: The compile source says home.dealcomplink was a WRDS Excel download converted to SAS, then reads its match fields.
The compile source reads DealScan facilities/packages, amendments, pricing, lender shares and covenant tables.
The compile source uses Compustat quarterly, annual and company data.
evidence.quote:
*get quarterly compustat data for SLACK computation;
   *definitions are from Table 4 of Demerjian and Owens;
proc sql;
   create table compq
   as select GVKEY,
             CIK,
	     	    intnx('QTR',yyq(FYEARQ,FQTR),0,'END') as FDATEQ format date9. label="Fiscal Quarter",
			    datadate,
			    ACTQ/LCTQ as CRTO label="Current Ratio",
			    (RECTQ+CHEQ)/LCTQ as QRTO label="Quick Ratio",
             (DLTTQ+max(0,DLCQ))/(ATQ-LTQ) as DBNW label="Debt to Equity",
			    (DLTTQ+max(0,DLCQ))/(ATQ-max(0,INTANQ)-LTQ) as DBTNW label="Debt to Tangible Net Worth",
			    (DLTTQ+max(0,DLCQ))/ATQ as DBAT label="Leverage",
			    ATQ-LTQ as NW label="Net Worth",
             (ATQ-max(0,INTANQ)-LTQ) as TNW label="Tangible Net Worth",
             DLTTQ,
             max(0,DLCQ) as DLCQ,
             ATQ,
             NIQ,
			    OIBDPQ,
			    XINTQ,
             INTPNY
   from compm.fundq(where=(indfmt = 'INDL' and datafmt = 'STD' and popsrc = 'D' and consol = 'C' and FYEARQ >= 1985 and missing(datacqtr)=0))
   order by gvkey,fdateq;
	quit;




*bring in the SIC code, which will be used if computing industry standard deviations for denominators;
proc sql;
   create table compq
   as select compq.gvkey,
             compq.CIK,
	          compq.FDATEQ,
	          compq.DATADATE,
			    input(SIC,4.) as SIC,
			    compq.*
   from compq left join compm.company
    on compq.gvkey = company.gvkey;
	quit;

*bring in senior debt and rent expense, which only appear to be available on the annual files;
proc sql;
   create table compq
   as select a.*,
             max(0,b.DS) as DS,
             max(0,b.XRENT) as XRENT
   from compq as a left join compm.funda(where=(indfmt = 'INDL' and datafmt = 'STD' and popsrc = 'D' and consol = 'C')) as b
   on a.gvkey = b.gvkey
    and year(a.fdateq) = b.fyear;
   quit;

evidence.quote:
Finally we examine if the decision to disclose PERF COV EARNINGS was triggered by

signing of new contracts or by making amendments to existing contracts. To test this, we

examine the contract initiation dates for each firm in our sample, specifically focusing on the

contract that was effective when the first voluntary disclosure of PERF COV EARNINGS was

made. We are able to identify the effective contract dates for 118 of our 128 firms. Of these 118

firms, only 24 (about 20%) signed contracts (or amendments to contracts) that became effective

in the 90 days leading up to the first voluntary disclosure. More than 25% of our sample had over

500 days between the contract date and the first voluntary disclosure. The mean number of days

between most recent contract and first voluntary disclosure is about one year. Thus, it does not

appear that firms are choosing to disclose because of changes to the terms of the debt contract.

actions.description: Obtain the exact author-prepared collection and supplemental input files referenced by the SAS code.
steps: Request both redacted Google CSV collection exports and the third-round Excel workbook; also request NWDATA, STREET, SLACK.SLACKDATA_04JUN2013, home.cstatviolations_nss_20090701, and DVW.COMPLETEPFSAMPLE/DVW.PFSAMPLE.
For each file, ask for its field definitions, identifiers, units, sample dates, importer settings and storage/libref location; preserve each distinct file as a separate source.
Place supplied files only in the author-confirmed locations after confirming permitted access; do not reconstruct missing collection records.
validation: Run a bounded metadata/readability check on received files and compare fields/keys/date coverage with the source joins.
Confirm the three bank-data rounds and each supplement cover the author sample; one-row readability does not prove full history.

actions.description: Obtain the exact author-prepared Compustat–Dealscan link or a documented compatible route.
steps: Request the historical Excel/SAS dealcomplink file described in the source and its creation/version notes.
Confirm its GVKEY, BCOID/DSID, FACID, SMBL_H, FACSTARTDATE and FIC fields, matching rules and period coverage.
Use only the author-confirmed link file/route; do not rebuild it from raw vendor data without an author-supported specification.
validation: Inspect the delivered file with bounded metadata tools and confirm required fields and coverage before joining it.

actions.description: Confirm authorized WRDS access and map the current vendor products to the authors’ legacy SAS names, fields and study periods.
steps: Confirm subscriber affiliation and product entitlements for LSEG DealScan, Compustat, CRSP and IBES; WRDS terms limit use to authorized users of subscribing institutions.
Ask WRDS support or the data steward to map current product schemas to DEALSCAN.*, COMPM.*, COMP.*, CRSP.COMPHIST/CCM/stock records, and IBES.IDSUM/STATSUMU/ACTPSUMU.
For local catalog candidates, separately verify source vintage and full history; do not treat one-row probes, product names or catalog misses as evidence of complete availability.
Retain the author filters/identifiers and do not silently substitute a neighboring dataset when fields or dates differ.
validation: After access confirmation, inspect schemas and covered dates for every jointly required table, identifiers and return/earnings fields.
Confirm the remote SAS librefs and actual dataset names before any later authorized execution.

actions.description: Resolve SAS startup, macro-loading and remote-library configuration from the environment owner/authors.
steps: Have the environment owner explain or resolve the TKELS Launch Service Load Failure and confirm SAS 9.4/SAS Connect availability; the probe does not establish license or entitlement.
Confirm how the separate WRDS.sas macro is loaded, where `%wrds` is defined for both entry files, and the remote location for the supplied WT.sas include.
Confirm remote HOME/DEALSCAN/COMPM/COMP/CRSP/IBES libraries and the client-side DVW/SLACK paths left blank in the distributed source.
Document which side owns each input/output directory and the authorized sign-on method.
validation: Repeat a standalone SAS startup/version probe and confirm SAS Connect separately.
After configuration review, verify each needed libref resolves to metadata for the expected datasets before any author code is run.

actions.description: Obtain the missing analysis programs or complete procedure for the paper’s result tables and figures.
steps: Request the Stata analysis programs or full step-by-step specification for all reported analyses, including the MI variable set, regression model, estimation/pooling commands and output targets.
Confirm the exact version of JAR_R2_FINAL_10MAR2016 used as analysis input and identify any further author-prepared files.
Keep analysis separate from the supplied SAS data build; do not add an analysis_only route until compatible prepared inputs and executable instructions exist.
validation: Map each table/figure to a supplied entry point, exact inputs and outputs; verify that the five-imputation method and model are reproducible.

actions.description: After all inputs, access, software and configuration are resolved, preserve the documented producer-consumer order.
steps: Prepare author inputs and confirm remote/local librefs under authorized WRDS/SAS setup.
Run Compile DealData 20DEC2014.sas first and confirm DEALSCAN.DEALDATA_22DEC2014 and ALLLOANS_22DEC2014 are written to the expected library.
Then run DVW JAR_R2 Version1 Data -- Public.sas; it consumes the DealData output and writes DVW.JAR_R2_FINAL_10MAR2016.
Only after the missing analysis workflow is supplied can the paper analyses be run against the confirmed output version.
validation: Before any later authorized execution, confirm every produced table and required downstream field/date coverage against the author specification.
Data generation alone does not establish reproduction of the paper estimates.
